Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

A Day of Atonement: Yom Kippur at Home

This agenda offers a warm and practical guide for observing Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish year, from the comfort of your home. It's a day dedicated to introspection, prayer, and renewal, culminating in a joyful break-fast.

  1. Late Afternoon

    Nourishing Before the Fast

    Prepare and enjoy a hearty, comforting meal to sustain you through the upcoming 25-hour fast. This is a time for family and quiet anticipation before the solemn day begins.

    Recipes: Classic Chicken Soup for Breaking the Fast · Kreplach for Yom Kippur

  2. Sundown

    The Sacred Silence Begins

    As the sun sets, the solemn fast of Yom Kippur commences. Don your white garments and tallit, and prepare for the Kol Nidre service, marking the official start of this holy day of atonement.

  3. Morning to Afternoon

    A Day of Prayer and Repentance

    Dedicate the day to introspection, prayer, and seeking forgiveness. Many spend this time in synagogue services, reflecting on the past year and committing to a better future.

  4. Just Before Sundown (next day)

    The Gates Close

    Conclude the day with the powerful Ne'ilah service, the final opportunity for prayer and repentance. The piercing blast of the shofar signifies the closing of the gates and the end of the fast.

  5. After Three Stars Appear

    Breaking the Fast with Joy

    As three stars appear in the sky, signaling the end of the fast, gather with loved ones to break the fast with a traditional, satisfying meal. Enjoy the flavors of renewal and the comfort of community after a day of profound reflection.

    Recipes: Classic New York-Style Bagels · Yom Kippur Lox and Bagel Platter · Sweet Noodle Kugel · Classic Cheese Blintzes · Classic Sweet Tea

May your day of atonement be meaningful, and your new year filled with blessings and peace.
